failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Agent answered with a word or entity already in the clue, or a longer form, instead of the bare head. 'McCormick & Company' (corporate suffix rule), 'Treaty of Paris (1815)' for a 'his' pointer (answer Napoleon), 'Transit of Venus' where the clue already says Venus.

rejected_edits.content: - Pronoun-led clues ('She played Tina Turner on the big screen & Rosa Parks on TV', 'He wrote...', 'Her home is now a museum', 'The 1815 Treaty of Paris was signed after his final defeat at Waterloo') ask for the PERSON (or group) the pronoun stands for, even without 'this'. A work, role, film, character, place, treaty, battle or event named in the clue or passages is evidence, never the answer. Find the person every passage ties to ALL the listed roles or deeds and give the plain 'First Last' name ('Angela Bassett', not 'What's Love Got to Do with It'; 'Napoleon', not 'Treaty of Paris'). A bare '<Title> <Full name>' clue ('Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah', 'President X', 'Prime Minister Y') asks for the country or body he led ('Brunei'), not 'Sultan of Brunei', the title or his name.
rejected_edits.target: - 'One of these <role/title>' ('the 14th one of these spiritual leaders') asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.

rejected_edits.content: - Aggregator pages (Search-ID, flashcard or quiz-site pages) often put the answer in the PAGE TITLE, with the clue repeated verbatim in the snippet ('fall - Search-ID.com' over a snippet repeating the clue; '[TLE] lenin - Search-ID [PAR] ...In 1927, this Russian leader's book "The State & Revolution" was banned in Boston...'). Treat a short title word that sits over a snippet containing the clue's distinctive words as the prime candidate ('fall', 'Lenin'), and sanity-check it against the clue. This works even when the context is only two short passages.
rejected_edits.target: Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.

rejected_edits.content: - Definition-style clues ('Sickle-shaped weapon of the Australian Aborigines', 'the sound a small object makes dropping into water, sometimes without a splash') have no 'this' pointer. Find the dictionary or encyclopedia page whose text paraphrases the clue ('the characteristic sound made by an object dropping into water without a splash'). The headword in its title ('Plop - definition of plop', 'Boomerang - Wikipedia') is the answer. Give that bare headword, without the category words the clue supplies ('sound', 'weapon'). A headword that recurs across several page titles beats a one-off word from a single passage.
rejected_edits.target: and answer with the common English name (Conch).
